lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: You've finally made it down to us, Polystratus. How long did you last? Nearly a hundred?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Ninety-eight, Simylus.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: And how did you spend the thirty years after I died? You were about seventy when I left.

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Extremely pleasantly. Surprising as that may seem.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: I find it very surprising. You were old, frail, and childless. How could you possibly enjoy life?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Well, for a start, I could enjoy everything. I had plenty of beautiful boys, exquisite women, perfumes, fragrant wines, and banquets that put Sicily to shame.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: This is news to me. I remember you as a complete penny-pincher.

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Ah, but all these luxuries poured in from other people, my friend. First thing in the morning, a crowd would gather at my door, and throughout the day I was showered with the finest gifts from all over the world.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: Did you become a tyrant after I died?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: No. I had thousands of lovers.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: [laughs] Lovers? At your age? With four teeth?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: I swear it! The most prominent men in the city. Old, bald, bleary-eyed, and snot-nosed as I am, they absolutely delighted in pampering me. If I so much as glanced at one of them, he thought himself blessed by the gods.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: Did you ferry Aphrodite across from Chios like Phaon, and she rewarded you by making you young and beautiful all over again?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: No, I was fiercely desired exactly as you see me.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: You're speaking in riddles.

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Oh, come now. You know this kind of love. It is the boundless passion people feel for rich, childless old men.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: Ah. Now I understand the source of your beauty. It came from 'Golden' Aphrodite.

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Still, Simylus, I had a marvelous time with my lovers. They practically worshipped me. I played hard to get, I locked them out of the house occasionally, and they just competed more furiously to outdo each other in their devotion.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: So what did you do with your estate in the end?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Publicly, I took each one aside and promised to make him my heir. He would believe me, and of course step up the flattery. But I had another, genuine will. I left that one behind, with instructions for the lot of them to go to hell.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: And who was the heir in the real will? A relative?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: God, no. A recently purchased Phrygian slave boy. Very pretty.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: About how old, Polystratus?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Twenty or so.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: Right. I think I know what he was doing to earn his keep.

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Well, he deserved the inheritance far more than they did. He might be a foreign scoundrel, but now those same prominent men are fawning over him. He got the money, so now he counts as an aristocrat. He shaves his chin and speaks broken Greek, but they're already calling him nobler than Codrus, handsomer than Nireus, and wiser than Odysseus.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: I couldn't care less. He can be commander-in-chief of all Greece for all I care, just as long as those flatterers didn't get a cent.
